# RustyNES v2.6.7 "Detent"

The bitstream becomes a release artifact, and a one-cycle disagreement is pinned to the cycle it happens on.

A detent is the notch that holds a mechanism at an exact position and makes that position repeatable. Both halves of this release are that: a bitstream that is published and reproducible rather than rebuilt from memory, and an assertion located to a single CPU cycle and attributed to a side.

**The emulation core is unchanged.** AccuracyCoin 141/141 (RAM decoder) and nestest 0-diff hold by construction; the work is in the sibling repository and in the release machinery.

## The gate

| # | criterion | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the bitstream is reproducible | **byte-identical `.rbf` from a clean tree and from an incremental build**, md5 `537d64f1…` (seed 3); timing closed at every corner |
| 2 | the artifact is named and published | `RustyNES_MiSTer-vX.Y.Z.rbf`, committed to `releases/` and attached to the GitHub release on both repositories |
| 3 | publication is repeatable | `scripts/release-rbf.sh` + `scripts/check_timing.py` (self-tested, gated in CI) + a documented ceremony |
| 4 | the APU residual is **CLOSED** | the inhibit now clears the interrupt at write+3, the documented cycle; checkpoint streams 11 identical → **52** |
| 5 | the checkpoint gate is registered | **51 goldens** (35 explicit + the 16 instruction ROMs, which ride the bus gate's own DUT run), mutation-proven, with its blind spot stated |
| 6 | no co-simulation regression | **123 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** — from 87 at v2.6.6, carrying **51 checkpoint comparisons** where that release had none, and the first run with nothing skipped |

## What is published, and what is not claimed

**No hardware has run this bitstream.** A booting core, a synced display, audible audio and a working controller are **not** claimed. What the co-simulation ladder does establish is per-cycle agreement with a 141/141 emulator on the declared compare surfaces, and AccuracyCoin agreement entry for entry across all 146 entries.

What it cannot reach **by construction**: the PPU gate compares the *pre-palette* index and the APU gate compares *per-channel integer levels*, so the palette, the video timing constants, the audio's absolute level and its band-limiting all sit downstream of every gate. That partition is deliberate — it is what stops a palette difference masquerading as a rendering one — and its price is that those four properties have no evidence behind them until a board runs the file.

v2.6.6 produced a bitstream and withheld it on the reasoning that a `.rbf` a user might flash should not ship on a compile alone. That is reversed here, for two reasons. The MiSTer distribution mechanism reads `releases/RustyNES_MiSTer-vX.Y.Z.rbf` out of the *repository*, so an empty `releases/` does not describe a cautious core — it describes an undistributable one, withheld from precisely the people who own the boards this project does not have. And a claim nobody made is not the same as a claim marked unverified; only the second is usable. The caution moves from an absence into a disclosure.

## A published number is withdrawn

v2.6.6 stated worst setup **+0.363 ns** and worst hold **+0.245 ns**. Two compiles of the byte-identical committed configuration — one from scratch with `db/`, `incremental_db/` and `output_files/` deleted, one incremental — produce a byte-identical bitstream and **neither reproduces those numbers**.

The innocent explanation was checked first, because Quartus reports four corners and quoting the wrong one would have explained everything:

| corner | worst setup | worst hold |
|---|---|---|
| Slow 1100mV 100C | +0.385 | +0.166 |
| **Slow 1100mV −40C** | **+0.108** | +0.046 |
| Fast 1100mV 100C | +3.106 | +0.096 |
| **Fast 1100mV −40C** | +3.543 | **+0.042** |

No corner produces either value, so the pair came from a build that is not the committed configuration — almost certainly one made before the seed was pinned, recorded, and never re-measured. The build itself **is** reproducible, and that is now evidence rather than an assumption.

(Those figures are v2.6.6's *configuration*, re-measured. v2.6.7's own build carries the Workstream B RTL fix and is reported at the end of this document.)

**The gate was also reading the wrong corner.** It inspected only Slow 100C, which is not the binding corner on this design: a bitstream failing at Slow −40C would have passed the release check while it reported three times the real margin. Corners are now discovered from the report by pattern.

## The checker was wrong twice, and mutation found both

`check_timing.py` first located both summary tables, extracted **zero rows**, and reported "no negative slack" — a pass earned by parsing nothing, because the rows begin four lines after the title rather than two. Fixing that exposed the second: with every data row commented out it reported **fourteen** clocks instead of zero, having run past the closing rule into the Recovery and Removal tables. It now bounds the scan to the three rules that fence a Quartus summary, treats an unparsed table as a failure, and ships a `--self-test` that CI runs and the release script runs before trusting its verdict.

## The one-cycle residual: measured, refuted, then closed

Caveat C2 asked whether a one-cycle difference was a trace observation point or a real assertion difference. **Both, for different cycles.**

The first was an observation point. The harness built its record after **eight of a CPU cycle's twelve** master clocks while the oracle reads its `_at_high` at end-of-cycle; `IRQ_PROBE_CYC` showed the frame-counter IRQ asserting on the **final edge** of cycle 29,827. Fixing it took checkpoint comparisons from **3 to 11**.

The second was real, and **the obvious fix was refuted by experiment before the right one was found**. A `$4017` write schedules four effects, and this core landed all four together at the sequencer's maturation: zeroing the frame counter, committing the mode, applying the inhibit, and clearing the interrupt. Moving all four one cycle later — to match the oracle *and* nesdev *and* a comment two lines above the constant — dropped blargg's 2005 APU battery from **11/11 to 4 of 11**, and among the seven that broke was `04.clock_jitter`, the ROM written to probe exactly that timing.

That refutation is what pointed at the answer. It says the *sequencer's* maturation is where the ROMs want it, so the thing on the wrong cycle had to be one of the other three at the same site. Separating **only the interrupt clear**, one cycle later, lands it at **write + 3** — nesdev's figure for a write made on an APU cycle — while the frame counter's zeroing stays put. Two effects of one write, on two different cycles.

Measured on `01-basics`, where the divergence lived: the CPU writes `$4017 = $C0` at cycle 116,842, and the line now holds asserted through all twelve master clocks of **116,845** and clears on its final edge. 116,842 + 3 = 116,845, and the oracle's own record reads `irqLo=1, irqHi=0` there. Both instruments agree, **on the documented cycle**, which is what makes this a fix and not a fit.

**What it closed:** checkpoint streams go from **11 identical to 52**, of 58 — all sixteen `instr_test-v5` ROMs, all eleven blargg APU ROMs, and the three checkpoint-7 stragglers.

**Why this is not the compensation trap.** v2.5.7 is the cautionary case: a phase was wrong and every window compensated. Here the interrupt *set* path was already correct — `01-basics` passes **655 of 655** checkpoints and those windows contain many set events — so a global phase error would not localise to one edge of one signal.

**Controls, both held.** blargg stays **11 of 11**, and the per-cycle bus gate still matches on **all 2,680,239** overlapping cycles: the CPU-visible behaviour is unchanged, which is exactly what moving an already-deasserting line by one cycle should look like.

## The seed is raised, and named

The fix adds one register to the frame counter and moved placement enough to land the framework's HDMI path at **−0.007 ns** at Slow 100C — seven thousandths of a nanosecond, inside `sys/`, on logic the change does not touch. The `.qsf` has anticipated this since v2.6.6 and prescribes raising the seed and disclosing it rather than re-running until it passes silently.

**Seed 3 is what this release publishes**, and every corner closes:

| corner | worst setup | worst hold |
|---|---|---|
| Slow 1100mV 100C | +0.138 | +0.240 |
| **Slow 1100mV −40C** | **+0.086** | +0.153 |
| Fast 1100mV 100C | +3.008 | +0.129 |
| **Fast 1100mV −40C** | +3.556 | **+0.096** |

`End Point TNS` 0.000 on all 56 rows, 0 errors, three distinct warnings, none citing this project's RTL.

## The gate that says what it cannot see

The checkpoint gate is registered over **51 comparisons** — 35 explicit plus the 16 instruction ROMs, which ride the bus gate's own DUT invocation at no extra simulation cost. It compares a rolling hash of all **nine** observable fields where every other gate compares four — which is how `put_cycle`, `nmi_line` and the two `irq_line_*` samples came to sit written as constant `false` in every trace the harness had produced.

Inverting `put_cycle`'s polarity is CAUGHT. Pinning `nmi_line` to false is **NOT CAUGHT**, and that was classified rather than filed: **not one gated golden ever raises an NMI**, so the gate is structurally incapable of catching it. Saying so means a future NOT CAUGHT there is expected rather than rediscovered.

Trying to close that hole found a fourth divergence cluster. Only five goldens raise an NMI; of the four with a checkpoint stream, all fail, and the three `ppuvbl` ROMs fail at the *same* checkpoint — one cause, not three. They had never been measured, because the manifests record the path the *oracle* exported with, unreadable from this repository, and the ad-hoc scan skipped them into a tally line reading "26 skipped (no manifest or ROM)".

## A gate that was not gating, and what it found

`nestest` **skipped on every run anyone had ever done** — its ROM path had no default while the instruction battery's does. Giving it one exposed something bigger: `docs/rung3-ppu.md` records nestest as closed at **5,002,992 cycles** at v2.5.8, and the gate's own `NESTEST_CYCLES` default named that figure, while the committed golden was `--frames 2` — **59,562 cycles**. Two orders of magnitude shallower than the number every document quoted, so nothing had tested the claim since it was made.

Re-exported at 5,062,688 cycles, the DUT diverges: **19,224 of 5,002,984** compared cycles, first at **cycle 265,640** in `$C291`.

**It is not this release's APU fix.** The pre-Workstream-B RTL, run in a separate git worktree against the same golden, produces the *identical* 19,224 — so it is pre-existing, and the shallow golden is why nobody knew.

The gate now runs to **265,000**: just short of the first known divergence, which is named rather than hidden, and **4.4x** the coverage it had (264,992 cycles compared, against 59,554). Raising it past 265,640 is the work of closing the caveat, not a knob to turn. It is recorded as a caveat rather than left red for the same reason the six checkpoint goldens are in a deny list — a gate red for a known and unactioned reason decays into noise.

**What it probably is not:** every rung-3 PPU gate is exact, AccuracyCoin's status vector is identical entry for entry across all 146 entries, and blargg's two batteries are 11/11 and 16/16.

## Not closed

**Rung 6 stays open.** No DE10-Nano and no SuperStation One are attached to this machine — confirmed by checking the USB bus, serial devices, block devices and mounts, not assumed. Hardware bring-up moves to the first release after a board exists.

Also carried: the `$2006` v-copy delay depth is still under-determined (1–4 dots all close `Hybrid Addresses`; 8 and 12 fail), and two AccuracyCoin sub-tests remain unregistered because the oracle itself fails them.
